TWO KINDS live here, and the difference matters:
kind=exact-pin  — the manifest declares an exact version (no ^ or ~). Dependabot still
proposes bumps; the pin only forces each one to arrive as a reviewable
PR instead of resolving silently on npm ci. Being at latest is normal.
kind=held-back  — we are actively refusing an available newer version, normally via a
dependabot ignore: rule. These are the ones that rot: every entry MUST
carry a review_by, and the lint warns once it passes.
This register does NOT cover two neighbouring cases that have their own files:
- overrides forcing a consumer off its declared range -> <workspace>/.override-range-baseline.json

Produces the SARIF that eslint-sarif.yml uploads to GitHub Code Scanning. Installed --save-exact so the SARIF schema cannot drift underneath the upload step without a reviewed bump; a malformed or reshaped report degrades a merge-gated scanner rather than failing loudly.

A PostgreSQL major is a data migration, not an image-tag bump, and the one-line diff hides all of it. PGDATA initialised by 16 refuses to start under 18 ("database files are incompatible with server"), so every developer volume and production's — behind 133 applied migrations — needs pg_upgrade or dump/restore, and there is no upgrade runbook in docs/runbooks/. docker-compose.failover.yml:68 pins postgres:16-alpine DIRECTLY and runs pg_basebackup into continuous streaming replication, which requires identical majors and refuses rather than degrading. build.yml:293 tests against 16 and :943 names the 16 tag in the canary. Both docker-compose.yml:4 and docker-compose.production.yml:33 declare image: concordvoice-postgres:16-alpine, so bumping only the Dockerfile FROM ships an image whose tag says 16 and whose contents do not. PR #3210 was closed for exactly this; the ignore stops it regenerating every Tuesday. Lift when the upgrade is scheduled as its own piece of work — moving the compose tags, the failover replica, the CI service, the canary and a runbook in lockstep. PostgreSQL 16 is supported upstream until November 2028, so nothing forces the date.

Ubuntu interim releases (YY.10, odd-year YY.04) get 9 months of support, so a bump to one ships a deploy-test base image that is end-of-life within the year. #3879 proposed 25.10, past its July 2026 end of life, after #3842 (26.04) was closed with `@dependabot ignore ubuntu major version`. The ignore lists the interim tags explicitly because dependabot `versions:` cannot express non-LTS; LTS tags (24.04, 26.04, 28.04) still flow. Review when 27.10 nears: append the next interim tags, or retire the rule if the image moves off numeric tags.

semgrep 1.186.0 declares boltons~=21.0, and the lock does not override it, so 26.2.0 is outside what semgrep accepts and the install would run a combination semgrep does not support (the lock installs with --no-deps, so pip would not catch it). The ignore covers only the update types that the pin forbids, so bumps inside the range still arrive. Re-check when SEMGREP_VERSION moves: drop or widen the rule if the new semgrep accepts 26.2.0.
